issues.title: Language switcher block is an unlabelled navigation landmark region
issues.description_html:
Problem/Motivation

The language switcher block has a navigation landmark region navigation role, but the region has no accessible name.

An accessible name is not strictly needed for all landmark regions. However in situations where there are multiple landmark regions of the same type on the page, the best practice is to differentiate these with an accessible name. We already do this for our menu and breadcrumb blocks.

Proposed resolution

Add an aria-labelledby reference to the language switcher navigation landmark region, pointing to the nested visually-hidden heading. Follow the same pattern as we already use for menu blocks.

Remaining tasks

patch

User interface changes

Adds an accessible name to the language switcher navigation landmark region, so screen reader users can differentiate it from other navigation landmarks on the page.

API changes

None.

Data model changes

None.

issues.title: Improve the perceptibility of contextual link buttons
issues.description_html:
Problem/Motivation

  • The border of the contextual link button is rather light, in particular in light mode, where the background of the page is also white. The pencil icon appears on hover, but it still requires some cognitive effort to process that there is a button and that this button is clickable (See the table in https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1won35PxhRFexJYE8FmZ4DCNTo7xEAxC8... or contextual_links.xlsx.zip for more details).


  • The label for the contextual link is redundant and missing a context most of the time. For example on the frontpage in Olivero for Drupal CMS you have in the rotor in VoiceOver eight entries with Open configuration options, toggle button, two entries with Open latest configuration options, toggle button, and three entries that provide a specific context: Open Primary tabs configuration options, toggle button, A celebration of Drupal and open-source contributions configuration options, toggle button, and Open footer configuration options, toggle button. - This is moved to #3623711: Labels for contextual links are redundant and missing a context
  • In Forced Colors mode the contextual link buttons have no pen icon on hover, neither in Gin nor in Olivero. [#Icons are invisible]

Discussed and iterated on the issue with @mgifford, @the_g_bomb, @katannshaw, and @drupa11y

Steps to reproduce

  • Enable Media, Media Library /admin/modules
  • Check the contextual link buttons on either /admin/content/media-grid
  • For testing the issue in Forced Colors mode make sure that you’ve switched to dark mode before.

Previous sets also suggested that it could be tested "on the frontpage in Olivero."

Proposed resolution

  • Increase the color contrast for the border in light mode so it meets 3:1, so the button gets a higher affordance and gets easier noticed. Same for the dark mode, due to the thin border, the border looks kind of jagged (not sure if that is the right term in english) - it is simply not a clearly recognizable button.
  • Add context to the button label for screenreader users.
  • Consider showing the contextual button in the context of layout builder all the time: https://www.drupal.org/project/drupal/issues/3037742
  • Ensure that the pen icon is shown in Forced Colors mode on hover (related to [#Several icons and images are invisible in Forced Colors mode])

Problem/Motivation

  3. The slash doesn't flip for RTL

comments.author: kentr
comments.body_html:
I know I'm not even remotely a VoiceOver expert, so this is speculation based on some observations.

To me, it looks like VoiceOver VO Right Arrow is selecting them rather than focusing them. It doesn't look like the same thing as tabbing through interactive elements.

The only way to stop this with the current markup may be aria-hidden="true".

I was able to reproduce the black rectangular VO cursor moving onto the separators with VO Right Arrow.

But when I move onto a separator, the link that I just moved away from retains the blue focus indicator that normally follows the tab key. When I press ENTER, the browser follows the link that has the focus indicator.

To me, this means that the separators don't receive focus.

See the attached video 3583516-5-breadcrumb.480p.mov.

VO Right Arrow also allows selection of lists, paragraphs, and arbitrary text nodes, even when they aren't part of the tab order and have focusable="false". I couldn't find any documentation for focusable="false".

See the attached video 3583516-5-arbitrary-text-elements.480p.mov.

Here's a test codepen.

Another idea

@rkoller noted in the Gin issue that this doesn't happen in Olivero.

I think it's because Olivero does this with just empty blocks that have two right-angle borders rotated slightly. Doing something like that would also be an option here (a single-sided border rotated slightly).

Olivero's CSS:

.breadcrumb__item {
    &:nth-child(n + 2)::before {
        display: inline-block;
        width: 0.5rem;
        height: 0.5rem;
        margin-inline: 1rem 1.25rem;
        content: "";
        transform: rotate(45deg);
        border-block-start: 2px solid var(--color--gray-45);
        border-inline-end: 2px solid var(--color--gray-45);
    }
}

comments.author: luissousa21
comments.body_html:
MR !16871 changes the strong element to a span in core/themes/default_admin/js/vertical-tabs.js.

Confirming @kentr's point in #5 that this is only an HTML tag change, the bold is already set in CSS, so there is no visual difference. .vertical-tabs__menu-item-title is a class-only selector carrying font-weight: var(--admin-font-weight-bold), and --admin-font-weight-bold: 575 is defined on :root in css/_variables/variables-typography.css. I checked the computed value in a browser: it is 575 both before and after the change, because the strong was already being overridden to 575 rather than the user agent default of 700.

One thing worth flagging for scope. The same strong element with class vertical-tabs__menu-item-title is emitted in two other places:

  • core/misc/vertical-tabs.js
  • core/themes/claro/js/vertical-tabs.js

Neither of those has a font-weight rule for .vertical-tabs__menu-item-title. Claro has no rule for that class at all, and core/misc/vertical-tabs.css and stable9 only reference it inside :focus, :hover and .is-selected selectors. So in those two the bold comes from the user agent default for strong, and changing the element there without adding a font-weight declaration would silently unbold the tab titles.

I have left those alone, since this issue sits under #3585823, but they have the same semantic problem and would each need a CSS change alongside. Happy to open a follow-up if that would be useful.

comments.author: mgifford
comments.body_html:
I'm not sure this is the best approach, but worth putting it out for consideration. 


/* 1. Define variables for both modes */
:root {
  --control-disabled-text: #5C6670;
  --control-disabled-border: #87909A;
  --control-disabled-background: #E7E9EB;
}

[data-drupal-theme="dark"] {
  --control-disabled-text: #AEB6BF;
  --control-disabled-border: #76818C;
  --control-disabled-background: #30363D;
}

/* 2. Target only form-related elements to prevent affecting layout containers like .region-sticky__items__inner */
input:disabled, 
button:disabled, 
select:disabled, 
textarea:disabled,
[role="checkbox"][aria-disabled="true"],
[role="button"][aria-disabled="true"] {
  color: var(--control-disabled-text);
  border-color: var(--control-disabled-border);
  
  /* Layered background: Red line (gradient) on top of the dynamic background color */
  background: 
    linear-gradient(to top left, transparent calc(50% - 1px), red 50%, transparent calc(50% + 1px)),
    var(--control-disabled-background);

  /* CRITICAL: Allows the gradient to render on native checkbox/radio inputs */
  appearance: none;
  -webkit-appearance: none;
  width: 16px;
  height: 16px;
  border: 1px solid var(--control-disabled-border);
  display: inline-block;
  vertical-align: middle;
}

/* 3. Accessibility: Windows High Contrast Mode support */
@media (forced-colors: active) {
  input:disabled, button:disabled, [aria-disabled="true"] {
    forced-color-adjust: auto;
    color: GrayText;
    border-color: GrayText;
    background: none; /* Gradients are usually disabled in HCM for clarity */
  }
}

issues.title: Accessibility fixes for Admin theme's node add/edit sidebar toggle control
issues.description_html:
Problem/Motivation

From #3618906: [Meta] Forms sidebar accessibility issues

The toggle control shouldn't be rendered as a link with role="button".
If it's meant to function as a link (IOW, it's supposed to go somewhere usable) without JavaScript:
Render it as a standard link.

Either change it to a button or add role="button" in the JavaScript when the toggle behavior is added.

If it's not meant to function as a link without JavaScript, render it as a button.

The toggle control should be operable with the SPACE key, probably on keyup.
See https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-..., https://adrianroselli.com/2022/04/brief-note-on-buttons-enter-and-space.....

The accessible name (& probably the title attribute) of the toggle control probably shouldn't change according to the state. See #3093378: Use ARIA disclosure pattern for submenu buttons in vertical toolbar orientation for @andrewmacphereson's explanation of why.

Similar to the toggle control, the close button shouldn't be rendered as a link with role="button".
I can't imagine that is supposed to function as a link in any circumstance, so it should probably just be a button element. Probably not really an accessibility issue, now that I think about it. Just bad practice.

Proposed resolution

Changes to the entity edit form sidebar in default_admin:

  • Splits migration/js/sidebar.js into a sidebar-toggle SDC and js/edit-sidebar.js.
  • Toggle and close controls are now <button> elements.
  • Sets the open/closed state before first paint. The sidebar no longer flashes open.
  • Opening the sidebar no longer collapses Navigation when page content changes height.
  • Below 1024px, content under the overlay is inert. Focus moves into the sidebar, and Escape closes it.
  • Positions the sidebar with CSS variables. The sidebar no longer jumps on load or overlaps the top bar.
  • Saved width now persists after reload.
  • Resizing works after AJAX, with touch, and in RTL.
  • Hides the resize handle below 976px.

Testing instructions

Desktop (1024px or wider):

  1. Toggle the sidebar closed, then reload. It stays closed with no flash.
  2. Toggle it open, then reload. It stays open.
  3. Drag the handle to resize, then reload. The width persists.
  4. Confirm the sidebar top aligns with the bottom of the top bar.
  5. Expand a details element. Navigation does not collapse.
  6. Set dir="rtl" on <html>. Dragging outward widens the sidebar.
  7. Ensure the sidebar toggle control is a <button> element, with the appropriate aria-expanded attribute.

Between 976px and 1023px:

  1. Confirm the sidebar top aligns with the bottom of the top bar.

Mobile (below 976px):

  1. Open the sidebar. Focus moves to the close button.
  2. Press Tab. Content under the overlay is not reachable. Navigation and the top bar are.
  3. Press Escape. The sidebar closes and focus returns to the toggle.
  4. Close with the close button and with the overlay. The URL does not change.

AI Disclosure

I completed most commits with the help of Claude. It actually found some more bugs (including the RTL width drag bug). After every change, I went through and read the code. I frequently had it make changes (especially around positioning of the sidebar) to make the code more readable (although that area is still very complicated). All code has been manually reviewed by me.

issues.title: Inline form error summary link is broken on textarea/textfield widgets
issues.description_html:
Problem/Motivation

When inline_form_errors is enabled, there is a summary that is displayed at the top of the page in a status message, when the form has field errors.

It is supposed to contain anchor links to the relevant fields, for the user to click on and correct the error.

However, on the text_textarea and text_textfield widgets, the anchor link is broken. It links to #edit-foobar-0, which is an ID that doesn't exist on the page, instead of #edit-foobar-0-value, which is the actual form field element.

The root cause is that the errorElement function on those widgets doesn't point to the proper form value element.

Steps to reproduce

1. Ensure that inline_form_errors is enabled.
2. Create a text or text_long field to a node bundle.
3. Add a constraint to the field definition on the bundle.
4. Create and save a node with a value that triggers a constraint validation error on the field.
5. Note that the link in the error summary status message does not work.

Proposed resolution

Update the errorElement function to point to value.

issues.title: The active primary local task has a too low color contrast and shapeshifting compared to the active secondary local task
issues.description_html:
Problem/Motivation

I've opened that issue already over in the Gin queue: https://git.drupalcode.org/project/gin/-/work_items/3506311. Over the course of the last few days I was able to slowly catch up again after being out of the loop for the last few months except for my attendance in the weekly ux meetings.
